items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Dickie' as a travel companion ('guy I used to ride with on the little train') but does not explicitly identify him as the famous trombonist Dicky Wells. ctx.x: Well, now when you say you were playing on the levee, what do you mean by that exactly? Where were you playing?

Well, they had spots. I'll tell you what kind of club we had. We had a spot, a very small place. We had a four piece band, a good one, too. And I think Laurence gave us a lot of advice that helped us. The piano man was of a different view. So, the spots we had were (?) was music and a little food like spaghetti. And the Negro cook's name was Julia. I'll never forget her as long as I live. Rough times, rough years. One of my last jobs going from the roadhouses (.?.)
